record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: What should the right notion of quantum catalytic space be?

evidence.quote: Problem 25. What does quantum catalytic space look like?

artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 work titled "Quantum Catalytic Space" (Buhrman, Folkertsma, Mertz, Sanders, Škoda, Šunko, Tripathi) proposes a concrete definition of quantum catalytic logspace (QCL/QCSPACE), shows robustness under Turing-machine vs. circuit formulations, and proves inclusions such as QCL containing log-depth threshold circuits TC^1 and being computable in quantum polynomial time. This addresses the question in a substantial way, though further refinements (e.g., lossy/approximate variants, comparison with classical catalytic logspace) remain active research, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Quantum Catalytic Space (arXiv:2506.16324)
status_evidence.snippet: We codify a concrete definition of quantum catalytic logspace and explore the robustness of the definition; establish the relationship of QCL to various classical and quantum complexity classes.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a definition of quantum catalytic space and studies its robustness and relationships to other classes.

status_evidence.title: Quantum Catalytic Space - DROPS / TQC 2025
status_evidence.snippet: Quantum catalytic logspace can simulate log-depth threshold circuits TC^1 and can be computed in quantum polynomial time.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes basic complexity inclusions for the proposed quantum catalytic space class.
